headline: Restyle the subject. Keep the scene.
intro: An interactive computer-vision application that gives people control over where an artistic style appears: select an object, refine its mask, and preserve the surrounding image.
context: University of Michigan · Computer Vision course project · Sept–Dec 2022
role: I originated the idea and led the pipeline design, implementation, model evaluation, and final application integration.

hero.alt: Six-second before-and-after sequence showing the original black swan transitioning into the AdaAttN segmented style-transfer result.
hero.caption: Before/after summary assembled from the course report; not a live inference recording. The selected swan changes while its surroundings remain visible.

metrics.label: AdaIN stylization time
metrics.note: Mean of 600 transfers; excludes segmentation and compositing

question.title: What if a style changed only what you selected?
question.text: Whole-image stylization can overwrite details a creator wants to retain. I connected interactive object selection to neural stylization so the boundary of the edit becomes part of the creative workflow.

steps.title: Select with clicks
steps.text: Use positive and negative clicks to guide FocalClick and refine a foreground mask without tracing the object's entire outline.

steps.title: Compare stylizers
steps.text: Evaluate AdaIN, AdaAttN, IEContraAST, and PAMA using ArtFID and separate timing experiments to understand the quality–speed tradeoff.

steps.title: Compose selectively
steps.text: Combine the stylized foreground with the original background through the mask, retaining the surrounding scene.

gallery.alt: Progress presentation screenshot of a click-based object-selection interface, generated mask, and tower-styling example.
gallery.caption: The progress checkpoint pairs the selection interface with a mask and styling example. The unified application was completed later.
gallery.credit: Original team presentation, 1:35 · DAVIS / WikiArt imagery

finding.title: The fastest model was not the quality leader.
finding.text: AdaIN had the shortest measured stylization time; AdaAttN had the lowest ArtFID (27.419 versus AdaIN's 27.955). Separating those objectives made the model choice explicit instead of treating speed and visual quality as the same result.
